themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.52)—suggesting a sudden concentration of Uber/Lyft-related problems in Mott Haven/Melrose this week.
evidence: 5 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 4.52)
Emerging issue with no prior Reddit or local news coverage, suggesting grassroots frustration
Timing coincides with potential increase in ride-hail activity or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Interview residents about what specific complaints are driving the spike (unsafe driving, blocking lanes, excessive idling)
Check with TLC enforcement data to see if there's a corresponding pattern of unlicensed or rule-breaking operators in the district

themes_detail.label: Street Sanitation Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 7 this week and missed collection complaints hit 7 last week—both 600% above the 8-week baseline (1.0 per week)—indicating a potential systemic failure in sanitation services over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 7 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score: 4.24)
7 missed collection complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score: 3.33)
Converging signals across two related services suggest workforce shortage or route disruption
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if staffing shortages, truck breakdowns, or route changes are behind the surge
Interview residents about visible trash accumulation and impact on block conditions
Cross-check with community board to see if this aligns with persistent infrastructure complaints

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints skyrocketed to 5 two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1900% spike (z-score: 10.97, highest severity)—pointing to rapid, unmanaged proliferation of legal and/or illegal retail cannabis operations in the district.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Highest z-score of any complaint category, indicating unprecedented deviation from baseline
No prior Reddit discussions or local news coverage suggests this is breaking news in the neighborhood
reporting_angles: Map active cannabis retail licenses in CD201 via the Office of Cannabis Management and compare to complaint locations
Interview residents about the nature of complaints: unlicensed retailers, odor, loitering, youth access concerns
Investigate whether illegal operations are outpacing enforcement or if recent OCM licensing decisions are driving expansion

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 5 last week from a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 4.41)—suggesting a recent pattern of disruptive activity in neighborhood parks that may be concentrated around specific sites.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 4.41)
Converges with community board's repeated budget requests for park improvements and services
Suggests specific parks or time periods may be experiencing new noise sources (events, unsupervised gatherings, equipment)
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating the complaints and visit to observe activity and conditions
Interview Parks Dept about whether recent programming changes, maintenance work, or staffing reductions have contributed
Talk to park regulars and community members about what type of noise (music, amplified events, crowds) is disrupting use

themes_detail.label: Encampment and Homelessness Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 12 three weeks ago from a baseline of 1.9 per week—a 540% increase (z-score: 5.52)—reflecting a visible growth in unsheltered populations that aligns with the community board's ongoing requests for expanded homeless services.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 5.52)
Chronic community board budget request for 'Other requests for services for the homeless' indicates long-standing, unmet need
Lead poisoning complaints also spiked 3 weeks ago (500%), possibly indicating overlap with deteriorating housing/shelter conditions
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations and interview NYC DHS to understand why capacity or outreach is insufficient for CD201
Speak with unhoused residents about barriers to shelter access and recent drivers of street population growth
Examine whether lead exposure complaints are concentrated in areas with high encampment activity, suggesting housing quality issues
